mathematical_premises.scope: fixed-period Parseval cube-frame Edgeworth expansion at output zero for signature {1,1,-1}
new exact finite-period sign-segregated optimization, Pell O(r^-4) saturation, and exact dense rotation existence

new_claim.statement: Within the fixed-period sign-segregated Parseval cube-frame class, the exact first Edgeworth coefficient is c_r(k)=r[57/(8k)+3/(4(r-k))]/20. For alpha=(19-sqrt(38))/17 and c_*=(63+2sqrt(342))/160, c_r(k)-c_*=D(k-alpha r)^2/[20k(r-k)]. The Pell sequence p^2-38r^2=17 with k=(19r-p)/17 gives exact coefficient gap D/[20k(r-k)(p+r sqrt(38))^2]=O(r^-4). Exact entrywise-dense rotations approach the same coefficient while preserving nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}.

unresolved_implication: No proof that 3sqrt(2) is the unrestricted sharp constant; remaining witness mechanisms include changing/mesoscopic frames, arbitrary rough diffuse laws, shared intermediate leverage, off-zero modes, and extra active spectrum.
next_step: Test whether the first negative Edgeworth correction remains uniform for mesoscopic frame periods r=r(m), or construct a rough-law/shared-row family outside the periodic neighborhood that could overshoot 3sqrt(2).
